delta_review.summary: The single remediation commit adds active external observation, strict attempt projections, controller/rollback entrypoints, locking, live restore inspection and matching tests/docs. The smoke observation-import defect is closed, but the production controller still replays caller-authored evidence instead of performing live steps, and restore mutation still trusts caller production identity plus an unbound database socket. Full-PR reconciliation also found the required CSP/same-host redirect semantics absent.
delta_review.evidence: git diff/log for the exact previous-to-current range; direct call-graph inspection; 41 committed LP-05 tests; reviewer forged-bundle and caller-production-identity counterexamples; exact-head GitHub CI run 30766943275

finding_revalidation.evidence: scripts/lp05/smoke/run.ts now rejects every external --observations import and routes external requests through runExternalSmoke; contracts bind the current certificate to the exact hostname/time, and the exact-head negative tests pass.

State-specific null/binding validation is improved, but controller-cli supplies createEvidenceOracles with a caller-authored evidence bundle. The reviewer constructed a complete forged bundle and runDeployment returned DEPLOYED with zero external mutation calls. No code produces INTERRUPTED, while remainingSequence directly continues any persisted forward state, bypassing the advertised bounded resume transition.

PGHOST/PGPORT/PGDATABASE are now derived from isolatedTarget and checked before spawn, but the live Compose labels and live PostgreSQL connection are observed independently, and assertIsolatedTarget does not parse or actively inspect productionIdentity. The reviewer proved an incomplete caller production identity is accepted by the mutation guard.

independent_pass.summary: A separate fresh-context reviewer was unavailable under the current no-delegation execution constraint. The same reviewer performed a distinct second pass over all new child-process, network, persistence, state, lock and restore call sites; it independently confirmed PRR-002/003 and exposed PRR-004.

decision.rationale: Cycle 2 resolves caller-authored external smoke import and adds substantial contract/state/rollback coverage, but three exact-head blockers remain: the production controller can reach DEPLOYED from a hand-written evidence bundle without executing deployment operations; pg_restore safety still depends on untrusted production metadata and an independently observed loopback socket; and the public edge neither emits required CSP nor proves that HTTP redirects to the same HTTPS host. Green CI does not exercise these counterexamples.

summary: The Cycle 2 patch is materially safer and fully closes the original smoke-import forgery. It does not yet close the production execution trust boundary: exact-head local reproduction reached DEPLOYED using only caller-authored canonical records and no external mutation, while the restore guard accepted incomplete caller production identity. Full-PR reconciliation also found explicit AC 4 CSP and redirect semantics missing from both the edge and its smoke proof.

findings.title: Production controller replays caller evidence without executing deployment
findings.observation: The new deploy:lp05 entrypoint accepts a complete caller JSON evidence bundle and creates every forward oracle by parsing or projecting that bundle. No oracle runs preflight, backup, migration, Compose replacement/readiness, external smoke, isolated restore or live production-before/after inspection. verifyCompleteEvidenceBundle runs once before the journal loop and establishes only self-consistent declarations. A separate resume gap also remains: no production code creates INTERRUPTED, while remainingSequence directly continues persisted forward states without the one-resume/two-hour transition.
findings.trigger: Construct canonical external-shaped smoke, backup, restore, phase and database records with matching digests, then pass them to createEvidenceOracles/runDeployment without invoking any external operation.
findings.impact: The exact-head controller appends DEPLOYED and can be persisted as operational success without deploying, migrating, backing up, restoring or contacting the authorized origin. This defeats AC 11-16, the planned hand-written-PASS rejection, mutation recovery and bounded resume authority.

evidence.description: Reviewer supplied a fully hand-written closed bundle. runDeployment returned {currentState: DEPLOYED, externalMutationCalls: 0}.
controller-cli passes request.evidence to createEvidenceOracles, whose forward steps only parse and project bundle values.
remainingSequence resumes any forward state directly; production code only consumes INTERRUPTED and never produces it.
The only runDeployment test covers a preflight failure; there is no production-controller fresh/upgrade success or active fault-boundary execution test.
The approved plan requires the controller to execute and re-read all ten live phases, reject hand-written PASS, and permit only one explicit bounded resume.

findings.remediation: Make production oracles perform the authorized live reads/mutations and create/load immutable evidence themselves; do not accept a future-complete bundle as operational input. Re-read the target/candidate/database and each newly produced record before every transition. Persist an explicit INTERRUPTED transition on recoverable process interruption, require the single bounded RESUMING path, and make stale-lock reclamation race-safe. Keep pure constructed external fixtures outside the production parser/persistence path.
findings.verification: A hand-written but internally consistent full bundle must be rejected before any success transition; fresh and upgrade controller tests must show the ordered external call graph, one call per mutation, stop/rollback at every injected boundary, exactly one bounded resume and no DEPLOYED without actual active outputs.

findings.title: pg_restore live checks still do not bind the socket to the isolated container
findings.observation: The restore environment is now derived from isolatedTarget and mismatch checks occur before spawn, but the mutation boundary remains composable from unrelated facts. inspectLiveIsolatedTarget obtains container/volume labels by Compose project and separately connects to caller-declared loopback host/port/database for pg_control_system(); it never proves that socket is published by that inspected container. assertIsolatedTarget also does not parse or actively inspect productionIdentity, so an incomplete caller object supplies the production inequality baseline.
findings.trigger: Provide a safe-looking lp05-restore-* project for label inspection, point databaseHost/Port/Name at another loopback database ending _restore, declare that database's system identifier, and provide an unrelated or incomplete productionIdentity.
findings.impact: The exact pg_restore socket can be a database other than the inspected isolated Compose target. Because production identity is caller-controlled at mutation time, the hard AC 10/12 guarantee against wrong-database restore is not established before age/pg_restore starts.

evidence.description: Reviewer passed an incomplete caller production object containing only composeProject and three database inequality fields; assertIsolatedTarget returned successfully (CALLER_PRODUCTION_IDENTITY_ACCEPTED).
Docker labels and PostgreSQL system identity are read on independent selectors; no Docker port/network inspection binds databaseHost/databasePort to the selected container.
The mutation guard parses only isolatedTarget and compares it with unchecked caller production fields.
Mismatch tests inject an already combined observed record and therefore do not test that the live socket belongs to the inspected Compose container or that production identity is actively observed.

findings.remediation: Actively parse and inspect the exact production identity at mutation time, and prove the declared database socket is the inspected isolated container through an exact Docker port/network/container identity binding (or execute psql/pg_restore inside that exact container). Compare live project/container/volume/system/database identities against production and the generated restore record immediately before spawn.
findings.verification: An incomplete/fake production identity and a mixed safe-container/unrelated-loopback-database observation must fail with zero subprocess starts; tests must prove the actual pg_restore endpoint is the exact inspected container and every production identity is independently observed.

findings.title: Required CSP and safe redirect semantics are neither configured nor proved
findings.observation: AC 4 requires CSP and HTTP redirection to the same HTTPS host. deploy/Caddyfile sets HSTS, nosniff, frame and referrer headers but no Content-Security-Policy. The active smoke accepts any 301/302/307/308 from HTTP without examining Location, and verifySecurityHeaders does not require CSP. The committed passing adapter fixture supplies neither Location nor CSP, demonstrating that evidence can claim both security assertions without them.
findings.trigger: Return an HTTP 3xx with no Location or a Location on another host, and omit Content-Security-Policy from every HTTPS response.
findings.impact: A deployment can be marked externally healthy while cleartext entry does not safely reach the authorized HTTPS origin and while the explicitly required browser content policy is absent. This fails AC 4 and weakens the public edge security boundary.

evidence.description: The redirect check validates status only; security-header verification omits CSP.
The production Caddy configuration contains no Content-Security-Policy header.
The exact-head success fixture has no Location and no CSP header but still emits PASS with all 22 assertions.
Requirements mandate trusted HTTPS, same-host redirect and CSP acceptance proof.

findings.remediation: Add an application-compatible Content-Security-Policy to the production and test edge, require it in local/external security checks, and verify the HTTP Location resolves exactly to the authorized HTTPS hostname/path with no userinfo or downgrade. Keep negative fixtures for missing/wrong-host/downgrade redirects and missing/unsafe CSP.
findings.verification: The current no-Location/no-CSP fixture must fail; exact same-host HTTPS redirect and an explicit approved CSP must pass through both local candidate acceptance and external smoke.

required_actions.action: Replace caller-authored external smoke PASS with active authority-bound observation and certificate validation.
Replace bundle-backed production oracles with active live deployment operations and enforce explicit bounded interruption/resume before DEPLOYED.
Bind pg_restore to the exact inspected isolated container/socket and independently observe the production identity before mutation.
Configure and prove the required CSP plus exact same-host HTTPS redirect semantics.
